review_response_tasks.stem: Amir knows what he wants to say in an email to his host, but is unsure about its order and politeness. He can send a draft before Wednesday and wants explanations while comparing versions.
options: A

Route Desk helps visitors plan a one-day trip using buses and trains. Staff print a route map and write down fares so you can use the plan without a phone. It is open on weekday afternoons. Staff do not book hotels or teach conversation.
B

Talk Circle is an evening meeting with volunteer partners. Practise everyday questions in pairs and change partners during the session. It is for speaking together, not receiving written corrections. No travel booking service is offered.
C

Kitchen Welcome is a Sunday morning class for beginners. Learn to prepare a simple lunch, with ingredients and equipment supplied. Tell the teacher about food allergies before the class. You cook and eat there rather than take a written language lesson.
D

Library Start offers a short indoor tour each weekday morning. Learn where different books are kept and how to borrow them. A large-print guide is available, and the whole route can be taken without stairs. There is no cooking or language practice.
E

Draft Clinic meets online on Wednesday evening. Send a short email draft beforehand. A tutor explains how its order and tone could be clearer, while you compare the original and suggested versions. It is not a live conversation club.
F

Repair Basket is a Saturday afternoon workshop. Learn to sew on a loose button and mend a small tear in a cloth bag. Needles, thread and practice cloth are provided. You may bring your own item, but electronic devices cannot be repaired here.
